overview: Black answers 2.d4 with the waiting move 2...a6, perhaps planning ...e5 or ...d5 later, but White simply takes the centre. I am unsure of the mainline theory; reasoning from the moves, Black keeps a flexible, slightly passive set-up and White gets a free centre.

white_ideas.idea: Build the centre with Nf3 and Nc3 or e5 ideas
Use the extra tempo for development

black_ideas.idea: Reach a French- or Scandinavian-like set-up with ...d5 or ...e6

typical_structures.structure: White d4/e4 centre against a flexible Black set-up

character.notes: Neither side takes early risks; Black waits and White develops, so play stays balanced rather than forcing.

soundness.notes: The waiting ...a6 costs a tempo but Black remains solid enough to reach normal structures.

structure.notes: The centre is not yet decided, so the structure depends on whether Black plays ...d5 or ...e5.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom choose this move order, and it is mainly a surprise.

level.notes: A rare sideline with few fixed plans, played by intermediate players.
